propositions: The divergent_implementation axis is mis-calibrated: it fires on only 7.72% of plan-v3 findings despite being the sole hard-override axis never formally calibrated, and 90% of omitted-scope findings (the class it targets) are graded none despite real impact.

Replacing the ordinal none|low|medium|high grading with a closed Literal set (contradicts_reality, omits_required_site, incomplete_enumeration, none) — with semantic-specific flooring and a pressure-release valve — bounds new blocks to 81 at worst-case while rejecting a blunt production-severity floor that would destabilize the remediation-loop convergence property.

ADR-0054 mandates data-driven calibration from existing version-tagged corpus only, rejecting purpose-built LLM eval suites and bulk re-review as calibration instruments, narrowing ADR-0036's A/B clause to corpus replay and dogfooding.

The structural change requires DIVERGENCE_GRADE01 mapping and exclusion from generic _SEV01 loop, mirroring the oracle-kind precedent, so symbolic grades are not silently scored as 0.0 and the axis stops firing entirely.

Plan text must explicitly state the four named structural changes (add DIVERGENCE_GRADE01, add _DIVERGENCE_FLOOR_GRADES, introduce _PLAN_GRADED_AXES, exclude from _SEV01 membership test) because omitting them would invert the intent — the implementation already does this correctly but the plan artifact does not.

All prompt-side consumers (verifiers, G7, preambles) and every fixture using the retired ordinal grades must be updated; the Literal makes low|medium|high a parse error so a missed site breaks immediately.
